Question: Two men set out at the same time to walk towards each other from \(M\) and \(N,\) \(72\) miles apart. The first man walks at the rate of \(4\) mph. The second man walks \(2\) miles the first hour, \(2\frac12\) miles the second hour, \(3\) miles the third hour, and so on in arithmetic progression. Then the men will meet:
Solution:
The midpoint is \(72/2=36\) miles from either starting point. The first man reaches it after \(36/4=9\) hours, so check the second man's distance after those same nine hours.

His hourly distances increase by \(\tfrac12\) mile each hour. Thus his ninth-hour distance is
\[
2+8\left(\frac12\right)=6\text{ miles}.
\]
For an arithmetic sequence, the sum equals the number of terms times the average of the first and last terms: pairing the sequence with its reverse gives the same total in each pair of positions. Hence his distance in nine hours is
\[
\frac{9(2+6)}2=36\text{ miles}.
\]
At nine hours, both men are therefore at the midpoint. Before then, the first has walked less than \(36\) miles and the second has walked at most \(36\) miles, since he always moves forward. Their combined distance is consequently less than \(72\) miles, so they have not met earlier. They meet midway between \(M\) and \(N\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
